words.ex: In my aunt's smart home, the lights come on by themselves as soon as anyone walks into a room.
Engineers say interplanetary travel will only become practical when a trip to Mars takes weeks rather than many months.
So far, space tourism has been so expensive that only a handful of very rich people have paid to fly above the Earth.
Using nanotechnology, a lab in Tashkent has made a sun cream whose particles are too small to leave white marks on the skin.
After keyhole surgery on his knee, the team's goalkeeper was walking again within a few days, with only two tiny scars.
In the doomsday scenario shown in the documentary, the ice caps melt and many coastal cities disappear under the sea.
From the age of ten, Bobur believed his destiny was to become a surgeon, and he never once doubted it.
Twenty years ago, few people could foresee how quickly phones would change the way we shop and travel.
Moving from a quiet village in the Zarafshan valley to a noisy mega-city of fifteen million people was a huge shock for Elyor.
On the evening before the holiday, every road out of the city was completely gridlocked and nobody moved for an hour.
Because of the population explosion in the suburbs, the town council had to build three new schools in just five years.
In our biology lesson we discussed how genetic modification might help wheat grow in very dry soil.
Some shoppers refuse to buy GM food because they are worried about its long-term effects on health.
Doctors hope that gene therapy will one day cure some rare illnesses that children inherit from their parents.
Our knowledge of the human genome helps doctors understand why certain illnesses run in families.
The young architects envisage a city centre where cars are banned and everyone travels by electric tram.
Some scientists warn that designer babies, whose eye colour or height could be chosen by their parents, raise serious ethical questions.
The film imagines a future in which cloning lets rich people order an exact copy of their favourite pet.
Some sociologists blame long working hours for the breakdown of family life in big cities.
In many villages three generations still live under one roof, but in the city the nuclear family is becoming more common.
Because of globalisation, the same coffee chains and clothing brands can be found in almost every large city.
With video calls and messaging apps, the world has become a global village where friends on different continents chat every day.
Some astronomers listen for radio signals from deep space in case extraterrestrial beings are trying to contact us.
The gulf between the richest and the poorest families in the country has grown wider over the past decade.
To clean the air, the city council took drastic measures and banned all old lorries from the centre.
Our neighbours' new smart fridge sends a message to their phones when they are running low on milk.
Thanks to genetic engineering, a type of rice has been developed that contains extra vitamin A.
